Aquira API
https://aquira2go.kcbieng.org/Aquira_WebAPI/swagger/docs/v1
 
api_key
 
Explore
General API Overview:
Sessions
All session must start with a post to /session with a user name and password as described in the 'Session' Parameter section below (Click 'Model Schema' to see the actual format). Passwords are not encrypted, you should use a network level security scheme to secure your site such as SSL or a VPN

Cookies
When you initially connect to the site you will receive an ASP.NET session ID cookie. When you successfully post a session you will receive an additional Aquira_ID cookie. both these cookies should be included in all subsequent communication for this session.
Logout
To logout you issue a session/delete request as described below. The session cookies should then be expired.
Permissions and Roles
The logged in user gets the same permissions as if he was logged into any of the Aquira UIs. i.e. If he can't access a particular type/feature/entity in Aquira he will not be able to via the API. As well as contain the users entity model The response contains 3 other models:
  
  !!General Aquira Settings!!
 
  "AppSettings": {
    "WebApiVersion": "string",
    "AquiraVersion": "string",
    "ServerTimeZoneID": "string",
    "CurrencyDecimalDigits": "integer",
    "NumberDecimalDigits": "integer",
    "FirstDayOfWeek": "string",
    "CalendarWeekRule": "string"
  },

  !!Reserved!!
  
  "UserSettings": {
    "Data": "string",
    "ProfileID": "string"
  },
  
  !!Role Settings indicating if the user can edit/view entities etc !!
    
  "RoleSettings": {
    "Name": "string",
    "Proposals": {
      "AvailableAccountsOnly": "boolean", <--  !! is the user restricted to Default Accounts only see Contract overview !!
      "View": "boolean",
      "Edit": "boolean",
      "New": "boolean",
      "Copy": "boolean"
    },
    "Contracts": {
      "AvailableAccountsOnly": "boolean",
      "View": "boolean",
      "Edit": "boolean",
      "New": "boolean",
      "Copy": "boolean"
    },
    "Leads": {
      "View": "boolean",
      "Edit": "boolean",
      "New": "boolean",
      "Copy": "boolean"
    },
    "Prospects": {
      "View": "boolean",
      "Edit": "boolean",
      "New": "boolean",
      "Copy": "boolean"
    },
    "Clients": {
      "View": "boolean",
      "Edit": "boolean",
      "New": "boolean",
      "Copy": "boolean"
    }
Request Objects
All request objects can contain an optional 'name' parameter which will be returned in the response:

{
  "OperationSpecificData": some object or objects,
  "name": "string"         this will always be returned in the response
}
Response Objects
All responses return an object which always contains a Success and Error and name values:

  {
    "OperationSpecificData": some object or objects,
    "Success": "boolean",          true if the operation execution completed with no errors.
    "Error": "ErrorReasonCodes",   one of the Aquira API error codes.
    "ErrorName": "string",         textual name of the Aquira API code.
    "name": "string"               the name parameter as passed in the request object.
  }
  
General Entities
The intention is that every entity type in Aquira will be represented by api resource, for example Reasons:

../Reason/Operation1
../Reason/Operation2
The number of operations which appear simply depend on the completeness of that entity's API.
Uniqueness
Each entity type is guaranteed to be unique within it's own domain. That is to say only one tax group can have a name of 'GST' and an ID of 648. However a Reason may also have the same name and ID.

Finding entities
If you search or lookup by some text value then you are not guaranteed a single response as the text search performs a 'contains' operation. For that reason you should do an equals operation on the returned data to get the exact entity you need.

Lookup
This is the minimum level of implementation for most entities and allows you to apply that entity to another which depends on it, for example setting a TaxGroup on a Contract. All lookup responses are similar and are based on the basic response object described above, They all contain an array of 'lookup models' which contain the ID and Name of the entity. Lookups parameters typically support search and in some case also include filtering fields (see Reasons and Clients)

{
  "Data": [               Array of lookup models
    {
      "Name": "string",     The unique name of the entity
      "ID": "integer",      The unique numeric ID of the entity
    }
  ],
  ... standard response data
}
  
Search
Some entity types can be searched for, typically the search response contains much more data for a given entity compared to the lookup. These are known as data models and as well as containing lookup data also contain some summary data associated with the entity.

{
  "Data": [               Array of data models 
    {
      "Name": "string",     The unique name of the entity
      "ID": "integer"       The unique numeric ID of the entity
      .... summary fields
    }
  ],
  ... standard response data
}
  
Create/Load
At the time of writing only Clients and Contracts support creation of new entities. Call the Create method to create a new entity in memory. Any default values (as configured in Aquira global settings) will be applied and the entity model will be returned to you as the Entity value in a standard response object. You may Load and existing by using the Load/id URL. This will load an existing entity. the response object for Entity operations are all similar:

{
  "Entity": {
      "Name": "string",     The unique name of the entity
      "ID": "integer"       The unique numeric ID of the entity
      "Version": "longinteger" The version of this entity
      .... detailed field values
    }
  ],
  ... standard response data
}
  
All Modifiable fields are contained within FieldValue objects which tell you the current access that you have for that field. You cannot modify a field that does not have an access of ReadAndWriteAccess.
Update (PUT)
Contracts and Clients implement the put verb for updating of entities. As mentioned above you can only modify editable fields To prevent permission errors you should send sparse updates. That is the object should only contain those fields you wish to and are able to modify.

As well as a sparse entity model, the update parameter also contains a save flag. If Save is set to true and the entity is valid it will be saved to the database. If the UpdateResponse Error code is -16 the entity is Invalid. You should look at the 'Errors' text to see which fields need to be changed in order to meet the validation rules for that entity type.

ContractEntityResponse {
  "Errors": "string",         validation errors JSON if 'Error === -16'
  "Entity": { ...             entity model with updates applied
  }
  "Success": "boolean",
  "Error": "ErrorReasonCodes",
  "ErrorName": "string",
  "name": "string"
 }
The entity model in the response contains The current state of the entity in the server. You should replace you own model with this one to prevent synchronization problems. Note that changing one field can have a ripple down affect through the entity changing many more fields, this is particularly true of contracts.
Contract API Overview:
Edit/Cancel
Existing contracts are subject to edit locking to prevent 2 users modifying the same contract at the same time. So as well as create and load there are also Edit and Cancel methods: Calling Edit will request that the contract be opened for edit if allowed the EditAllowed values will be set to true. If editing is denied this will remain false and the EditingUser value will contain the ID and name of the person editing it.
Edit will Load the contract if it has not already been loaded.
A Loaded contract will be completely readonly until edit has been called.
Edit will return a contract with some fieldvalues writable depending on the contract status and user permissions
Calling PUT (Update) with Save==true with commit the contract to the DB and the contract will no longer be editable.
Calling PUT (Update) with Save==false updates the contract in memory and it will remain editable (as dictated by the edit rules).
Calling Cancel ends the contract edit and nothing is saved.
Newly created contracts are always editable.
Field Order and AvailableSelectionItems
In principle it is possibly to create a contract with only 2 requests, Create and Update. However the API business logic makes this impractical as there are numerous dependencies with a contract. This logic is represented by the AvailableSelectionItems object in the Contract Model. This object is populated when the Advertiser has been set, after which.

1. Advertiser Set. SalesReps is now populated. Also the following Available items come into play.
a Accounts. You can optionally select any other Account from the Account (client) lookup. Check the users Role setting to see if he is restricted to only accounts in this list
b. Agreements. You can optionally select any other Agreement lookup.
c. Brands. If there are no brands then this item is not editable.
2. Account Set
a. AvailableContacts lists any contacts set on the account. This is for the BookedBy text field. This field can be any value
3. Brand set.
a. The Contract Product will default to the Brand's product. (eg Brand: Toyota, Product will be Automobiles.
4. SalesRep selected.
a. Available RateCards will now be populated.
b. The RateCard object contains the RateCard version information.
c. If a SignDate has been only RateCard versions which are available will be included
5. SignDate set.
a. RateCardVersions in available RateCard is now filtered by signdate.
6. RateCard set.
a. Available Stations and Station groups are now populated.
b. These should be used in the Station/StationGroup pickers.

post /Agreement/Cancel/{id}
Cancel an agreement. This is not a true cancel, as an agreement does not have an edit mode. The cancel function will just unload the agreement.

Response Class (Status 200)
OK

The spotline load arguments

ModelExample Value

post /Contract/LoadSpotlineStationSpots
Load all the spotline details specific to a station's spotline(s).

Implementation Notes
Spotlines can contain large amounts of data so the contract will contain only spotline summary data. In order to see all the data you have to load the line you are interested in.

Response Class (Status 200)
OK

put /Contract/Put

post /Contract/Update
Update a contract which was created or put in edit mode.

Implementation Notes
If Save == true then the contract is submitted to the database otherwise it is updated in memory on the server only. the UpdateEntity must be sparse

Response Class (Status 200)
OK

post /Report/RunReport
Generate and load a non-direct report into memory. This operation will generate cache-control headers for the browser to use to determine length of time until the report is considered stale. It will also generate an eTag header that can be passed back to the server with future requests and used to determine if the response requires all data to be sent or a 304 status code to indicate that the resource has not changed. To always send back data, do not include the eTag in the request to this operation.

head /User/HeartBeat
Simply return an ok from the server. Used to test if the session has timed out. If it has, this action will never get run, as the AquiraAuthorizationFilter returns a 401 if the HttpContext.Current.Session[Constants.API] is null.

Response Class (Status 200)
OK
